name: Hanun
overview: Hanun was a male king of the Ammonites, a people descended from the tribe of Ammon. He held the unique position of ruling over the Ammonites during the time recorded in 2 Samuel 10. Scripture provides limited additional details about his life or character beyond his kingship and tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Hanun means 'favored,' reflecting a proper name without direct indication that it was given by God. His title, 'King of the Ammonites,' signifies his royal authority over the sons of Ammon, emphasizing his leadership role among his people as recorded in 2 Samuel 10:1.
familyAndRelationships: Hanun is explicitly identified as the son of Nahash, establishing a direct familial lineage within the Ammonite monarchy. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any further family relationships for Hanun.
scriptureSignificance: Hanun's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as king of the Ammonites during a critical period in Israel's history. His kingship situates him within the geopolitical tensions described in 2 Samuel 10, marking him as a key figure in the interactions between Israel and its neighbors. This highlights the ongoing challenges faced by God's people amidst surrounding nations.
